independence: Personally read complete blinded batch013 index4, then independently compared only StudyInstanceUID/Report columns from the archived train.csv and parent-provided current Kaggle copy. No013 annotations or gold target values were inspected. Whole CSV hashing/equality treated all bytes as opaque; no target columns were materialized. This audit used the existing kaggle_current copy and did not itself perform a new authenticated download.
findings: The313-character source has one explicit left-knee MRI heading, a clinical question and sequence protocol, followed by a short findings fragment. The findings end immediately after an unlocalized high-grade sprain phrase, without a named injured structure or completed descriptive conclusion.

The phrase about possible ACL injury is in the diagnostic question and remains a question, not a current finding. The ending does not establish which ligament or structure the high-grade sprain describes. No missing content can be reconstructed from surrounding clinical context.

The exact short report is present in both CSV copies and the blinded batch. The entire archived train.csv is byte-identical to the current Kaggle copy with matching SHA256. Therefore the observed source incompleteness was not introduced while producing this blinded batch or by this recovery copying step.

Given the parent-provided copy provenance, the same incomplete field exists in the current competition source snapshot. This does not identify where before that snapshot the apparent truncation occurred, prove that a longer original report exists, or distinguish an upstream export cut from an intentionally incomplete dictated note.

actions: Retain the source fragment and its identity binding unchanged.
Keep any target lacking sufficient anatomically localized source evidence masked; this technical audit assigns no clinical states.
Seek an authenticated longer report or verified upstream correction only if available; do not append guessed text, use the diagnostic question as a finding, or infer the missing structure.
Record source incompleteness separately from local aggregation corruption and from image decoding quality.

limitations: This establishes exact identity across the two supplied CSV copies and batch text, not completeness of the original clinical report.
No image/header inspection or clinical interpretation was performed for this source-completeness audit.
